name: KLAS Research: Healthcare AI Vendor Ratings from Provider Feedback
title: KLAS Research: Healthcare AI Vendor Ratings from Provider Feedback
answer: KLAS Research publishes healthcare IT research built on interviews with providers and payers rather than vendor claims. Its comparison pages rate clinical AI, payer data and AI platforms, and autonomous coding vendors, and its reports cover adoption, patient access automation and early markets. A solution qualifies only after at least two confirmations of work performed in the last three years, and scores come from a sample of recent clients, so the ratings reflect reported experience rather than marketing.

sections.body: KLAS Research publishes healthcare IT industry reports and vendor comparison pages, drawing on data captured in thousands of customer interviews. It publishes more than 70 reports a year, including the annual Best in KLAS performance rankings, Points of Light case studies on payer, provider and vendor partnerships, and Emerging Insights reports that give leaders an early look at new technology. The pages read include comparison pages for healthcare artificial intelligence data science solutions, payer data intelligence and AI platforms, and autonomous coding, plus an Emerging Company Spotlight on Assort Health and an overview of report types. Copyright notices on the pages read carry a 2026 date.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: KLAS defines healthcare artificial intelligence data science solutions as software providing machine learning or natural language processing in clinical, operational and financial areas. Machine learning products learn algorithms and statistical models to perform tasks without explicit instructions, relying on patterns and inference, while natural language processing handles large amounts of natural language data. Payer data intelligence and AI platforms unify clinical, member, operational and financial data for enterprise analytics, reporting, predictive modeling and AI-enabled decision support, presenting it through dashboards, scorecards and alerts for business and non-IT users. Autonomous coding is described as medical coding systems powered by AI that assign codes to charts with minimal or no human intervention. The Assort Health report describes AI automating and customizing inbound and outbound patient communication, integrating with EHRs and adapting to feedback to improve transparency, cost and patient experience. KLAS also links to reports on healthcare AI adoption, payer analytics platforms and an early autonomous coding market.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: KLAS publishes more than 70 reports each year. A solution needs a minimum of 2 confirmations of a service performed in the last 3 years to qualify for a comparison page. Reducing filters narrow the list of solutions rather than recalculating scores. Data comes from interviews with a sample of firms' recent clients and is not necessarily comprehensive. Performance scores may change significantly when newly interviewed provider organizations are added, especially with the small sample sizes of emerging markets. Findings are not meant to be conclusive data for an entire client base. Provider organization employees can create a free KLAS account.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: For a reader following AI in healthcare, KLAS offers a way to judge vendors on reported provider experience rather than vendor claims. Its category definitions set out what counts as clinical and operational AI, from machine learning and natural language processing to autonomous coding and payer decision support. The qualification rule of two confirmed engagements in three years, and the stated limits of sample-based scoring, tell the reader how much weight a rating carries. The linked reports point to where adoption and early markets stand, including patient access automation and autonomous coding.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Healthcare

sections.body: The pages read are largely category definitions, report listings and comparison pages, with the substantive findings held in the linked reports rather than reproduced. KLAS states its data comes from a sample of recent clients and is not comprehensive, that scores can shift with new interviews, and that findings are not conclusive for an entire client base. The Assort Health page is an Emerging Company Spotlight with a small number of live clients. Some pages consist mainly of account, login and cookie notices.
